hero.title: Crush Your WMAD Interview.
hero.subtitle: Everything you need to know to prepare, practice, and succeed as a C2 applicant.

guide.title: Three interviews stand between you and C2.
guide.subtitle: Each one tests something different — here's what to expect at every stage.

steps.title: Technical Interview
steps.description: You'll walk through core programming fundamentals and problem-solving out loud. Interviewers care more about how you reason through a problem than whether you get it perfectly right the first time.

steps.title: Motivation Interview
steps.description: A conversation about why you're here. Expect questions about your goals, what drew you to tech, and how you plan to handle the intensity of a bootcamp schedule.

steps.title: Teamwork Interview
steps.description: A short group exercise with other applicants. This stage looks at how you communicate, listen, and contribute when working toward a shared goal.

questions.title: Sample Questions
questions.subtitle: Tap a category to see the kind of questions that tend to come up. These are a starting point, not a script.

technical.name: Technical
questions: Walk us through how you'd debug a webpage that isn't loading its styles.
What's the difference between let, const, and var?
How would you center a div — name a couple of different ways?
Explain what happens between typing a URL and the page appearing on screen.
Given a list of numbers, how would you find two that add up to a target sum?

motivation.name: Motivation
questions: Why did you choose WMAD over other options?
What does success look like for you six months after this program?
Tell us about a time you taught yourself something difficult. How did you approach it?
What's pulling you toward tech specifically, rather than another path?
How do you plan to balance the intensity of this program with the rest of your life?

teamwork.name: Teamwork
questions: Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate. How did you resolve it?
How would you handle a group member who isn't pulling their weight?
Tell us about a time you explained something technical to a non-technical person.
What role do you naturally take on in a group project?
How would you respond to feedback on your code that you disagreed with?

tips.title: Tips from Students
tips.subtitle: Read tips from students who passed the exam.

cards.quote: Don't be afraid if you don't know the answer. Show that you can think and try your best.
cards.author: — C3 Student

cards.quote: fake it's until you make it. Show your reasoning and how you work through problems, not just the answer.
cards.author: — C3 Student

cards.quote: Work well with your team. Listen and help each other.
cards.author: — C3 Student

cards.quote: Sleep well before the exam. It helps you think better.
cards.author: — C3 Student

cards.quote: Don't be shy to ask questions. It shows you want to learn.
cards.author: — C3 Student

items.question: How long does each interview take?
items.answer: Each interview is short and focused — plan for roughly 15–20 minutes per stage. Check your invitation email for the exact schedule.

items.question: Can I use notes during the technical interview?
items.answer: You're welcome to think out loud and sketch things out. It's not closed-book — interviewers are more interested in your reasoning than a memorized answer.

items.question: What happens if I don't pass on my first attempt?
items.answer: Not passing one stage doesn't mean the door is closed. Reach out to the admissions team for guidance on next steps and future intakes.

items.question: What should I bring?
items.answer: A laptop if you have one, a notebook, and a few questions of your own for the interviewers. Comfortable, presentable clothing is fine — no dress code pressure.

items.question: How soon will I hear back after my interview?
items.answer: Results are typically shared within a week of your final interview stage. If it's been longer, it's worth checking in with admissions directly.

items.question: If I'm not good in English can I join WMAD?
items.answer: Yes! WMAD welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. We value your problem-solving skills, motivation, and willingness to learn over English proficiency. Many successful graduates started with limited English and improved throughout the program.
